role.altitude: From grading jobs, answering pay questions and building reports one at a time to owning Noordhaven's job architecture: the four-factor evaluation method, the AFAS job and pay data, and the evidence for every pay difference. The specialist designs and checks the pipelines that produce gap figures, draft grades and handbook text, and explains the results to the works council, managers and auditors.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: standard pay, headcount and career-path reports from the AFAS extract in Power BI
HR Administrator: keeping job scheme, job category and benefits fields in AFAS consistent
FP&A Analyst: costing CAO pay rounds, merit budgets and flex-worker pay scenarios
Learning and Development Specialist: building the Studytube modules on pay bands and pay transparency for managers
HR Business Partner: first drafts of answers to individual pay requests under the pay transparency law
role.ceiling_note: About 335 hours a year sit in these eight tasks; roughly 150 to 160 could be saved. The limits are legal and relational, not technical: grading and pay decisions need a human decision (GDPR Art. 22), grade or pay recommendations may become high-risk under the AI Act from 2 December 2027, the works council must consent to the evaluation system (WOR 27(1)(c)), and CAO jobs stay inside the sector's own grading system. Drafting a grade from a job description is only about 70% right in the one documented pilot, so every grade still needs the specialist's review.
skills_to_grow: Four-factor job evaluation (skills, responsibilities, effort, working conditions) and how to defend it in front of the works council
Reading and testing AFAS data extracts and Power BI models; basic SQL or Power Query
Writing and checking prompts and rubrics for LLM grading drafts, and measuring their error rate against expert grades
EU pay transparency directive, its Dutch implementation, AI Act Art. 26 duties and GDPR Art. 22 in practice
Explaining pay statistics, including gap figures with their legitimate explanations, to managers and employee representatives
role.ambitious_version: Noordhaven enters the pay transparency regime ready: every one of its jobs, including agency roles, has a current four-factor description and grade the works council has consented to; the unexplained pay gap per group is tracked monthly instead of yearly; every pay request is answered well within two months; and offer acceptance and 90-day retention are linked to band position, so pay decisions feed the hire-to-productive North Star.

tasks.short: Design and update our rules for pay, promotion and grading, and explain them to managers and the OR.

today.trigger: New law (pay transparency), a CAO change, a director's request, or recurring complaints about promotion or pay decisions.
steps: Collect current policies from SharePoint and the CAO texts
Look at what peers and the sector do, mostly through contacts and the internet
Write a policy proposal in Word with options
Discuss with the HR Director, HRBPs and Finance
Prepare a works council request for consent or advice and present it
drudgery: Comparing old policy versions and CAO articles by hand
Rewriting the same proposal for the director, the OR and managers
today.time_sinks: Finding and reconciling the current policy and CAO wording, then rewriting the proposal for each audience.

lenses.faster: A model compares current policy, CAO articles and the draft pay transparency bill and lists the gaps; the specialist starts from a structured draft instead of a blank page.
lenses.autonomous: When a CAO text or a new legal text lands in SharePoint, a job flags which Noordhaven policies it touches.
lenses.ambitious: Promotion and pay rules written down properly for all three sites and all job families for the first time, ready before the pay transparency law starts.
lenses.joy: Less hunting through old Word versions; more time on the actual design choices and the talks with the OR.
lenses.options: Three or four policy variants with their cost from AFAS data and their effect on the pay gap, instead of one proposal.
lenses.altitude: The specialist maintains a policy register linked to the CAO and the law and decides which changes to make, instead of rewriting documents.
reach: HR Business Partner: manager-facing explanation of promotion rules
FP&A Analyst: cost of policy variants

tasks.human_edge: Choosing what is fair at Noordhaven, weighing site and union relations, and winning works council consent.
tasks.pattern_why: The output is a policy choice that needs judgment and negotiation; AI speeds research and drafting but cannot own the decision.

in_practice.trigger: New legal or CAO text published, or a policy review on the HR calendar.
steps: Model reads the new text and current SharePoint policies and lists affected clauses
Specialist sets goals and constraints
Model drafts two to four variants with a plain-language summary
Excel or Power BI costs each variant on AFAS data
Specialist chooses, edits and takes it to the HR Director and works council
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist and HR Director approve the proposal; the works council consents where WOR 27 applies.
systems: Microsoft 365 Copilot or a comparable LLM
data_needed: CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer and warehouse CAO texts
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint policy library with version history and the decision memo.

evidence.claim: The Dutch pay transparency bill requires a job evaluation system on four factors, with works council consent on system, criteria and grouping.
A pay or grading system needs works council consent unless a CAO settles it.
LLMs can compare policy texts and draft policy variants well enough to save drafting time.

risks: Drafts copy generic or foreign practice that does not fit the CAO
Policy text looks finished and gets less scrutiny than it needs
Pay data sent to an external model without a processing agreement (AVG)
research_questions: How many hours per year actually go to policy drafting versus meetings and OR consultation?
Does the works council accept AI-drafted proposals if the source documents are shown?
Which policies are fully settled by the CAO and so out of scope?

tasks.short: Run the appraisal and equal-pay programs: yearly review cycle, pay gap checks, follow-up with managers.

today.trigger: The yearly review and merit cycle, and from 2028 the yearly pay gap report under the pay transparency law.
steps: Prepare appraisal forms and the timetable for managers
Chase managers to finish reviews
Pull pay data from AFAS into Excel and check differences by gender and job
Discuss outliers with HRBPs and managers
Report outcomes to the HR Director and works council
drudgery: Rebuilding the same Excel pay gap analysis every year
today.time_sinks: Manual Excel gap analysis and email chasing during the cycle.

lenses.faster: Gap figures per job category come straight from the AFAS extract in Power BI; reminders to managers go out on schedule without the specialist.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly job recalculates the gap per group and flags any category over 5% that has no recorded explanation.
lenses.ambitious: Track the unexplained pay gap monthly, including agency workers, and close it well before the first report over 2027 pay, due 7 June 2028.
lenses.joy: No more rebuilding the gap spreadsheet; the time goes to understanding why a difference exists and fixing it.
lenses.options: Several correction scenarios (spread over one, two or three years) with their cost and resulting gap.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the gap model and the explanation register and checks its logic, instead of running the numbers.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: gap dashboard
HR Administrator: appraisal cycle reminders

tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a pay difference has a legitimate reason, and the joint evaluation with the works council if it does not.
tasks.pattern_why: The gap figures are deterministic, but the program itself is run with people; AI prepares the numbers and drafts, the specialist leads.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly AFAS extract refresh and the yearly review calendar.
steps: Power BI recalculates pay gap per job category and gender from AFAS
Rules flag categories over 5% without a recorded explanation
Model drafts an explanation note per flag from job and pay history
Specialist reviews with the HRBP and records the decision
Yearly report built from the same data for the works council
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist decides on every explanation and correction; the HR Director signs the report.
data_needed: AFAS pay, job scheme and job category fields
Agency pay data from the three staffing agencies
in_practice.logs_to: Gap explanation register on SharePoint, kept for the joint evaluation and audits.

evidence.claim: An unexplained gap of 5% or more after six months triggers a joint evaluation with the works council; agency workers count.
AFAS Profit 8 stores job schemes and categories as preparation for pay transparency.
Power BI can recalculate gap measures nightly from an AFAS extract.
evidence.source: model knowledge; Power BI is already in use at Noordhaven

risks: Agency pay data incomplete or late, so the gap figure is wrong
Small groups make figures identifiable (AVG)
Explanations drafted by a model accepted without checking
research_questions: Are AFAS job scheme and category fields filled for all 1,200 employees?
Will the three staffing agencies deliver pay data in a usable format?
How large is the current gap per job category?

tasks.short: Keep the staff handbook, benefit rules and pay-related records in AFAS current.

today.trigger: CAO change, new benefit, legal change (e.g. pension transition) or an error found in AFAS.
steps: Find the affected sections in the SharePoint handbook
Rewrite the text and check it against the CAO
Update job, pay scale or benefit fields in AFAS
Ask HR Administrators to correct individual records
Publish and announce the change
drudgery: Searching all handbook sections that mention a changed amount or rule
Checking AFAS records one by one
today.time_sinks: Finding every place a rule appears and checking records manually.

lenses.faster: A model finds every handbook passage affected by a CAO change and drafts the new text; an AFAS check lists records that do not match the new rules.
lenses.autonomous: When a new CAO or pension fund document is filed, the draft handbook update and the AFAS mismatch list are ready the next morning.
lenses.ambitious: One handbook per site in Dutch and the main languages of the warehouse staff, always in line with the CAO.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses searching Word files for an old allowance amount.
lenses.options: Plain-language and full legal versions of the same section side by side.
lenses.altitude: The specialist approves changes and maintains the source-of-truth rule set, not the text.
reach: HR Administrator: record corrections
Payroll Specialist: checking pay-scale tables before the month close

tasks.human_edge: Judging how a CAO article applies at Noordhaven and signing off what employees will rely on.
tasks.pattern_why: Several steps across SharePoint and AFAS with exceptions; the text is rights-bearing so a person approves before publishing.

in_practice.trigger: New CAO, pension or policy document saved in the SharePoint source folder.
steps: Agent compares new document with handbook and lists affected sections
Agent drafts revised sections with tracked changes
Script checks AFAS pay scale and benefit fields against the new rules
Specialist reviews, edits and approves
Publish on SharePoint and send corrections to HR Administrators
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves each changed section and each batch of AFAS corrections.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint version history and an AFAS change log.

evidence.claim: Pensioenfonds Vervoer expects its new scheme on 1 January 2027, which will require handbook and record changes.
LLMs can find affected passages and draft revisions with tracked changes in Word.

risks: A wrong amount published becomes a claim from employees
Draft misses a CAO exception for one site
Translated versions drift from the Dutch original
research_questions: How many handbook changes per year, and how many hours each?
Is the handbook a single source on SharePoint or several copies per site?
How often do AFAS records disagree with the CAO tables today?

tasks.short: Build reports: org charts, career paths, pay and grade analyses for management.

today.trigger: Requests from the HR Director, Finance or the works council, and yearly pay review.
steps: Export data from AFAS or the Power BI extract
Clean and combine it in Excel
Build charts and tables
Write a short explanation
Send in PowerPoint or Excel
drudgery: Cleaning exports and fixing job titles
Redrawing org charts after every reorganisation
today.time_sinks: Data cleaning and rebuilding the same report formats.

lenses.faster: Standard reports and org charts are generated from the nightly AFAS extract; the specialist only writes the commentary.
lenses.autonomous: Org charts and pay-band reports refresh every night; changes over a threshold are flagged.
lenses.ambitious: Career-path maps for warehouse and transport staff showing the next grade, required certificates and pay, for the first time.
lenses.joy: No more retyping job titles into PowerPoint.
lenses.options: Several cuts of the same data (site, job family, flex versus own staff) without extra work.
lenses.altitude: The specialist defines the data model and report logic and checks it, rather than building each report.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: standard pay and headcount reports
Learning and Development Specialist: certificate requirements per career step

tasks.human_edge: Choosing what the report should say and noticing when a figure is implausible.
tasks.pattern_why: Structured AFAS data, fixed rules, checkable output; built once with AI coding help and run without a model.

steps: Power BI model recalculates pay, grade and headcount tables
Org chart generated from manager fields in AFAS
Career-path report links jobs, grades and Studytube certificates
Exceptions (missing manager, missing grade) listed for correction
Specialist adds commentary for ad hoc requests
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist checks the exception list and any report going to the works council or board.
systems: Visio or Power BI org chart visual
data_needed: AFAS employee, job, grade and manager fields
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI refresh history and report versions on SharePoint.

evidence.claim: Power BI is already refreshed nightly on an AFAS extract at Noordhaven.
Org charts can be generated from HR data with standard tools such as Visio Data Visualizer.

risks: Bad manager or grade fields in AFAS produce wrong charts
Pay reports reach people without the right access (AVG)
research_questions: How many reports per year are repeat formats versus one-off questions?
How complete are manager and grade fields in AFAS?
Does Studytube data link to AFAS employee numbers?

tasks.short: Study what jobs really require, how they relate, and how roles change, to grade them correctly.

today.trigger: New or changed job, regrading request, or reorganisation; pay transparency preparation.
steps: Interview the manager and job holders
Observe the work on the warehouse floor or in transport
Write or update the job description
Compare with similar jobs and the CAO grading system
Propose a grade
drudgery: Writing job descriptions from interview notes
Comparing against dozens of existing descriptions
today.time_sinks: Turning notes into a structured description and comparing with other jobs.

lenses.faster: A model turns interview notes into a description on the four factors and proposes a grade with reasons; the specialist checks it.
lenses.autonomous: A quarterly scan compares AFAS job data and Recruitee vacancy texts with job descriptions and flags drift.
lenses.ambitious: Every non-CAO job at Noordhaven described and graded consistently before the pay transparency law starts.
lenses.joy: Less writing up notes; more time on the floor understanding the work.
lenses.options: Draft grades under two or three evaluation methods to show where they disagree.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the job architecture and the grading rubric, and audits model drafts.
reach: Recruiter: consistent job descriptions for Recruitee vacancies
HR Business Partner: input for reorganisations

tasks.human_edge: Seeing the actual work, judging accountabilities, and deciding whether a change is material enough to regrade.
tasks.pattern_why: Unstructured notes to a structured description and per-factor grade, inside a fixed evaluation process with the specialist deciding.

in_practice.trigger: Regrading request or new job in AFAS.
steps: Specialist interviews and observes, records notes
Model drafts description and per-factor grade with reasons
Model lists the three closest existing jobs and their grades
Specialist decides and records the reasons
Grade stored in AFAS job scheme
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist decides every grade; CAO jobs stay in the CAO system.
in_practice.logs_to: Job evaluation file on SharePoint with draft, decision and reasons; logs kept six months or longer per AI Act Art. 26.

evidence.claim: ChatGPT models graded 50 job descriptions per HERA factor with over 70% accuracy against experts.
61% of employers are rewriting job descriptions for AI and 49% say salary structures lag.
Do not regrade if core accountabilities have not materially changed.
Grade recommendations can be high-risk under AI Act Annex III 4(b) from 2 December 2027.

risks: Roughly 30% wrong drafts become unexplained pay differences if not caught
Anchoring: specialist accepts the draft grade
High-risk AI Act duties apply, including informing the works council first
research_questions: How accurate are draft grades on 30 Noordhaven jobs against the specialist's grades?
Which jobs fall under the CAO system versus Noordhaven's own?
Will the works council consent to AI-drafted grades with human decision?
What is the outcome of the CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer regrading?

tasks.short: Decide what job analysis tools we need and build questionnaires and interview guides.

today.trigger: Preparing a job evaluation round, new evaluation method, or pay transparency.
steps: Review existing questionnaires and the evaluation method
Draft questions per factor
Test with a few managers and staff
Revise and translate
Get works council input
drudgery: Rewording questions for different job groups
today.time_sinks: Drafting and redrafting questionnaire versions per job family.

lenses.faster: A model drafts questionnaires and interview guides on the four factors per job family, in plain Dutch and other languages.
lenses.autonomous: Answers from Microsoft Forms are summarised per job automatically for the evaluation file.
lenses.ambitious: Job analysis for all job families including agency roles, using short mobile questionnaires on the warehouse floor.
lenses.joy: Less time on wording; more on testing whether questions reveal the real work.
lenses.options: Several questionnaire versions to test with a pilot group.
lenses.altitude: The specialist designs the evaluation instrument set and checks its validity.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: survey design and analysis
Learning and Development Specialist: skill inventories

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which questions are fair and valid for drivers and warehouse staff, and getting OR agreement.
tasks.pattern_why: The instrument is a design choice that needs validation and consent; AI drafts and summarises.

steps: Specialist sets goals and factors
Model drafts questionnaire and interview guide per job family
Pilot with a small group via Microsoft Forms
Model summarises pilot answers and unclear questions
Specialist finalises and presents to the works council
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves the instrument; works council consents to the evaluation system and criteria.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint project folder with instrument versions and pilot results.

evidence.claim: Job evaluation under the pay transparency bill uses skills, responsibilities, effort and working conditions.
LLMs draft and translate questionnaires and summarise free-text answers.

risks: Questions biased toward office jobs
Translation errors change meaning
Pilot answers contain personal data (AVG)
research_questions: Which job families have no current job analysis instrument?
Do warehouse staff complete mobile questionnaires at useful rates?
What does the works council require to consent to the instrument?

tasks.short: Analyse pay and workforce data and supply figures to management, CBS, pension fund and sector bodies.

today.trigger: Requests from management, CBS surveys, pension fund and sector fund data deliveries, salary surveys.
steps: Read the request and its definitions
Pull data from AFAS and agency portals
Calculate in Excel
Check against previous submissions
Submit or present
drudgery: Mapping AFAS fields to each external form
Reconciling agency hours with own data
today.time_sinks: Mapping definitions and reconciling sources for each request.

lenses.faster: Recurring submissions are mapped once and produced from the AFAS extract; a model reads new request forms and proposes the field mapping.
lenses.autonomous: Recurring deliveries are prepared on schedule and wait for approval.
lenses.ambitious: Market pricing and CAO costing for every pay round, with findings drafted per job family.
lenses.joy: No more re-reading survey definitions every year.
lenses.options: Several costing scenarios for a CAO round or benefit change.
lenses.altitude: The specialist maintains the mapping library and checks submissions, not the calculations.
reach: FP&A Analyst: CAO costing
Controller: personnel cost figures

tasks.human_edge: Interpreting definitions, judging what may be shared externally, and explaining results.
tasks.pattern_why: Several sources and steps with exceptions; outputs leave the company so a person approves.

in_practice.trigger: Scheduled delivery date or new request in Outlook.
steps: Agent reads the request and maps definitions to AFAS fields
Script calculates figures from the AFAS extract and agency data
Agent compares with prior submission and flags large changes
Specialist reviews and submits
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint submission archive with mapping and figures.

evidence.claim: Compa Analyst Agent with Mercer data drafts market-pricing findings.
Agencies must supply pay data for agency workers under the pay transparency law.

risks: Wrong definition mapping gives wrong external figures
Personal data shared beyond what is needed (AVG)
Market data cost not justified for 1,200 employees
research_questions: How many external submissions per year and how many hours each?
Is market data needed beyond the CAO tables for office jobs?
Can agency portals export pay data in a stable format?

tasks.short: Build and give training on pay bands, benefits and pay transparency for managers and staff.

today.trigger: New policy, pay transparency preparation, new managers, or benefit changes like the pension transition.
steps: Decide the learning goals
Write slides and handouts
Give sessions on each site
Answer questions afterwards
Update materials
drudgery: Rebuilding slides for each site and audience
Answering the same questions by email
today.time_sinks: Making materials and repeating sessions on three sites.

lenses.faster: A model drafts slides, cases and a Studytube quiz from the policy; the specialist checks and gives the session.
lenses.autonomous: New managers get the pay-band module in Studytube on their start date in AFAS.
lenses.ambitious: Every manager trained on answering pay requests and setting offers within band before the law starts.
lenses.joy: Less slide-building; more live discussion with managers.
lenses.options: Role-play cases of pay conversations at different levels of difficulty.
lenses.altitude: The specialist designs the learning path and measures whether managers apply it.
reach: Learning and Development Specialist: module building in Studytube
HR Business Partner: manager coaching on pay talks

tasks.human_edge: Teaching in the room, handling hard questions about fairness, and building trust with managers.
tasks.pattern_why: Drafting materials is fast with AI, but the training is given by a person who answers questions.

in_practice.trigger: Policy change or new manager in AFAS.
steps: Model drafts slides, cases and quiz from the policy
Specialist edits and checks
Module published in Studytube; session planned on each site
Specialist gives the session
Questions collected and used to update the material
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves the content before publishing.

evidence.claim: Pay ranges must be shared before negotiation and pay requests answered within two months.
A benefits chatbot must tell users it is AI.
LLMs draft slide decks and quizzes from policy documents.

risks: Errors in the material spread to all managers
Training shows generic rather than Noordhaven rules
research_questions: How many managers need pay transparency training and by when?
Can Studytube enrol automatically from AFAS start dates?
Do managers who took the module answer pay requests correctly?
